content.headline: Devoted to God and our neighbor.
content.subheadline: Grace Church is an independent Reformed church in Laguna Niguel, committed to the faithful preaching of the apostolic gospel. You are welcome here this Sunday.

$media.alt: Grace Church's brick sanctuary with a cross above olive trees

content.headline: Hear the Word preached
content.intro: Sunday mornings we are preaching verse by verse through Isaiah, and Sunday evenings through 1 John.

content.headline: This week at Grace
content.intro: Worship, study, prayer, and fellowship through the week. Subscribe once and every gathering shows up in your phone's calendar.

$media.alt: Pastor James Wenger

children.text: I'm so glad you've come to learn a little more about us. Grace Church of Laguna Niguel is an independent Reformed church. We are committed to the faithful preaching of the apostolic gospel.
We hold to the traditions and theology of the reformers and take great pleasure in discovering God through His Word. You are invited to join us this Sunday as we worship our Triune God.

content.headline: Find your place
content.intro: We work hard to make Grace a place where everyone who comes can connect with God and with each other.

content.text: For the eyes of the Lord range throughout the earth to strengthen those whose hearts are fully committed to him.

content.headline: Join us this Sunday
content.body: Adult Sunday school at 9:00 am, morning worship at 10:00 am, and evening worship at 6:00 pm.

$media.alt: The walk to the Grace Church sanctuary under olive trees

data.title: Plan your visit
data.intro: We are a church committed to Jesus Christ and the historic teachings of the Christian faith. We would love to have you join us this Sunday.

content.headline: Sunday at Grace
content.intro: Services begin promptly, and ushers are glad to help you find your way.

items.title: A warm welcome
items.body: You will be greeted with warm smiles and an open door. Ushers are ready to help you find what you need and answer any questions you have.

items.title: Worship guided by Scripture
items.body: Our services include prayer, the reading of Scripture, preaching, singing psalms and hymns, giving, confessing our faith with the Nicene Creed, and the Lord's Supper every week.

items.title: Come as you are
items.body: We worship our God reverently and joyfully. Dress in whatever feels most comfortable to you.

items.title: Families worship together
items.body: Children of all ages are welcome in the service. There is also a nursing mothers' room, a nursery, and children's classes through 5th grade.

$media.alt: A teacher with children at a craft table in a Sunday school classroom

children.text: The nursery (Room 101, birth to age 3) is open before the service begins.

Older children start in the sanctuary with their families and are dismissed to their classes just before the sermon. Grades 1 through 4 come back for the Lord's Supper and sit with their families; PreK and kindergarten stay in Room 104 until the service ends.
Every lesson points children to Christ, and each class reviews the First Catechism or the Westminster Shorter Catechism.

items.question: What kind of church is Grace?
items.answer: We are an independent Reformed congregation that seeks to glorify God and enjoy Him forever. Our statement of faith is the Westminster Confession of Faith with the Larger and Shorter Catechisms.

items.question: When and where are services?
items.answer: Sunday morning worship is at 10:00 am and evening worship is at 6:00 pm, at 24600 La Plata Drive in Laguna Niguel. Adult Sunday school meets at 9:00 am.

items.question: What is the evening service like?
items.answer: The Sunday evening service runs from 6:00 to 7:00 pm, with a time of prayer, songs, and a sermon. There is no childcare in the evening.

items.question: How can I get connected?
items.answer: Start by joining us for worship. From there you will find a monthly fellowship meal on the first Sunday after the service, weekly community groups, men's and women's studies, youth and young adults groups, and ways to serve in the church and the community.

items.question: Can I watch online?
items.answer: Yes. Sunday services stream live on our YouTube channel, and recent sermons are on the sermons page.

content.body: Questions before you come? Call the church office or send us a message.

data.title: About Grace Church
data.intro: A group of believers bound together through a common faith in the Lord Jesus Christ, and firmly committed to the authority of God's Word.

$media.alt: The congregation standing to sing during Sunday worship

children.text: Grace Church of Laguna Niguel is an independent Reformed church committed to the exegetical teaching of God's Word. We hold to the traditions and theology of the reformers and take great pleasure in discovering God through His Word.
Our hope is to serve you as you seek to grow in the grace and knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. Call the church office any time, or come and see us on Sunday.

items.title: Christ-centered preaching
items.body: At Grace you will be nourished in the Word through a deep commitment to Christ-centered, expository preaching, verse by verse through books of the Bible.

items.title: Led by elders
items.body: Grace Church is led by a plurality of pastors and elders under the authority of Jesus Christ, the Chief Shepherd.

items.title: A historic confession
items.body: Our statement of faith is contained in the Westminster Standards, and every Sunday we confess our faith together with the Nicene Creed.

items.title: Life together
items.body: Fellowships, community groups, and studies fill our weekly and monthly calendar, so deep and lasting friendships can grow within the church body.

content.headline: What we believe
content.body: We accept the Scriptures as our only authority in matters of faith and practice.

$media.alt: A Bible open to the book of Isaiah

data.title: What we believe
data.intro: For the word of God and for the testimony of Jesus Christ. Revelation 1:9

children.text: Our statement of faith is contained in the Westminster Standards: the Westminster Confession of Faith, the Larger Catechism, and the Shorter Catechism.
We accept the Scriptures as our only authority in matters of faith and practice. Our doctrine may be summarized as follows.

We believe in the Scriptures of both the Old and New Testament as being verbally and plenarily inspired by God, inerrant and infallible in the original writings, and of supreme and final authority in matters of faith and practice (Matt. 5:17-18; Prov. 30:5-6; 2 Tim. 3:16-17; 2 Pet. 1:20-21; John 10:35; Luke 16:17).

We believe God is a Spirit, in and of Himself infinite in being, glory, blessedness, and perfection; all-sufficient, eternal, unchangeable, incomprehensible, everywhere present, almighty, knowing all things, most wise, most holy, most just, most merciful and gracious, longsuffering, and abundant in goodness and truth. We believe in the Holy Trinity: there are three persons in the Godhead, the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, and these three are one true, eternal God, the same in substance, equal in power and glory, although distinguished by their personal properties (Deut. 6:4; Isa. 45:5-6; Ps. 90:1-2; Gen. 1:1; Matt. 28:19; Eph. 4:4-6; John 15:26; 16:15; 1 Pet. 1:2; John 1:1; 20:28; Heb. 1:8; Phil. 2:6; Acts 5:4, 9).
We believe that Jesus Christ was begotten by God, conceived by the Holy Spirit, and born of the virgin Mary (John 1:1-14; Matt. 1:18-25; Luke 1:26-38; Isa. 7:14).

We believe in the Holy Spirit, the third person of the Trinity, the Lord and giver of life, who convicts the world of sin, righteousness, and judgment. He empowers the preaching and teaching of the Gospel and applies the benefits of Christ's saving work in the life of believers (John 14:16; 16:7-11; 3:5-8; 1 Cor. 12:13; Titus 3:5; Eph. 1:13; 4:30; Rom. 8:9-11; Gal. 5:16, 22-25).

We believe that mankind was created in the image of God, both male and female, in a state of righteousness, knowledge, and holiness, yet mutably so. They sinned, through their own free will and the temptation of Satan, and thereby incurred not only physical death but spiritual death, which is alienation from and enmity with God, and human beings are born with a sinful nature which renders them incapable of saving themselves (Gen. 1:27; 5:1; 1 Cor. 11:7; Rom. 6:23; 3:10; 8:7; Gal. 3:22).

We believe that the Lord Jesus Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures as a representative and substitutionary sacrifice, and that all who believe in Him are justified through faith alone, apart from works, on the basis of His shed blood and perfect righteousness (2 Cor. 5:14-21; 1 Cor. 15:3, 22; Heb. 4:15-16; Rom. 5:8; 1 John 2:2; Gal. 2:16; 3:11; Rom. 3:23-26; 4:5-8, 25; 8:33).

We believe in the bodily resurrection of our crucified Lord on the third day, His appearances to His disciples, His ascension into heaven, and His present life there as High Priest and Advocate for us, having been given all authority in heaven and on earth (Luke 24:23-40; 1 Cor. 15:12-23; Acts 1:1-11; 1 Pet. 3:22; Heb. 4:14; 7:25; 8:1-2; 9:11-15).

We believe in the blessed hope and the personal, visible return of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ at the end of the age (Titus 2:13; Rom. 8:18-25; 1 Pet. 1:7, 13; 2 Thess. 1:7; Acts 1:11; Mark 13:33-37; Matt. 24:42-51).

We believe that all who receive by faith the Lord Jesus Christ have been born again by the Holy Spirit, have been forgiven of their sins, and are adopted by God and made heirs of eternal life (Rom. 10:14, 17; Eph. 2:8-10; Titus 3:5; John 1:12-13; 3:3-8; Ezek. 36:26; 2 Cor. 5:17; Rom. 8:14-17; 1 John 3:2).

We believe in the bodily resurrection of the just and the unjust at the return of Christ, the everlasting conscious suffering of the lost in hell, and the fellowship of the saved in heaven (1 Thess. 4:13-18; 1 Cor. 15:51-58; Rev. 20:11-15; 21:8, 27; Matt. 25:31-46; Luke 16:19-31; 2 Cor. 5:6-9; Phil. 1:23; John 14:1-6).

We believe in the existence of a personal devil, who is still working in the world to destroy the souls of men, and that he and all his angels and all who do not receive Christ as their personal Savior will eternally perish in the lake of fire (Isa. 14:12-15; Rev. 19:20; 20:10, 14-15).

We believe in the Church, whose mission it is to preach the Scriptures to all the world, all of its endeavors being guided by a parity and plurality of elders and supported by the wise stewardship of God's people (Eph. 1:22-23; 5:23-32; Col. 1:18; Matt. 28:18-20; Acts 14:23; 20:28-31; Titus 1:7; 1 Pet. 4:10; 1 Cor. 16:2; 2 Cor. 8:24-9:15).

We believe that the sacraments of the Church, given by the Lord, are Baptism and the Lord's Table (Communion) (Rom. 6:3-4; Acts 2:38-41; 8:12, 36-38; Matt. 28:19-20; 26:26-30; 1 Cor. 10:16; 11:23-30).

data.title: Membership
data.intro: We believe it is biblical for Christians to commit themselves to a local church, and for that church's leaders to shepherd them.

children.text: In the membership class you will learn about the vision of Grace Church, our leadership, our doctrinal statement, how to become involved in ministry, and the privileges and responsibilities of church membership.
Classes are held once a year. Contact the church office to ask about the next one.

items.title: Membership is biblical
items.body: While the term is never used, the concept is implicit throughout the New Testament: believers identified with a specific local body and devoted themselves to it (Acts 2:42; Heb. 10:25; Rom. 12:5; 1 Cor. 14:12, 26).

items.title: It helps the elders shepherd
items.body: Membership helps the leaders of the church fulfill their God-given task of shepherding, and identifies disciples who build and sustain its ministries (Gal. 6:10; Heb. 13:17).

items.title: It strengthens you
items.body: Membership moves each of us out of the vague cloud of good intentions and into the clear light of committed participation (1 Cor. 12:7).

items.title: Commit
items.body: Pledge yourself to the local body of Grace Church.

items.title: Celebrate
items.body: New members are presented at a worship service so the whole church can rejoice together.

content.headline: Interested in membership?
content.body: Let us know and we will tell you when the next class meets.

data.title: Privacy
data.intro: How this site handles analytics, videos, and the information you send us.

children.text: This site uses anonymous, cookieless analytics to understand which pages are useful. It does not set cookies, store identifiers in your browser, or build a profile of you.

When you send the contact form, we store your name, email, phone, and message so the church office can reply. We do not sell or share this information. The form is protected by Cloudflare Turnstile, which checks that a person, not a bot, is sending it.
Sermon videos load from YouTube only after you press play. The live page shows YouTube's player directly, and YouTube's own privacy policy applies to it.
Online giving takes you to Cornerstone, which has its own privacy policy.
To ask about or delete information you have sent us, use the contact form and mention this page.

data.title: Living in the Light of God's Grace
data.summary: God's grace calls His people to godly living, and because of the Servant's work the Lord welcomes outcasts to Himself.

children.text: Read Isaiah 56:1-8.

The Bible makes clear that we are saved by grace alone through faith alone in Christ alone. Does it then matter how we live? Some say it does not; this is known as antinomianism. What is antinomianism?
In verses 1 and 2 we see that God's grace calls us to godly living: to keep justice and do righteousness. What is justice, and how do we keep it?
What is righteousness? What is the difference between positional and practical righteousness?
In verse 2 the Lord points to the need to keep the Sabbath. In principle, what is the Sabbath?
What is the origin of the Sabbath? Why was the day we observe it changed under the New Covenant?

Because of the work of the Servant (chapter 53), the Lord now welcomes outcasts to Himself (verses 3 to 8). What did the Servant of the Lord, Jesus Christ, do to accomplish this? See Ephesians 2:11-16.

God welcomes all to Himself because of the work of Christ, and He requires those who come to Him to keep His commandments. Why does He require obedience if our obedience has nothing to do with our salvation?
What practical application can you make from this text and sermon?
Pray!

data.summary: Care and Bible teaching for children from infancy through 5th grade during Sunday morning worship.

$media.alt: Children at a craft table with their teacher

children.text: Parents can keep their children with them in worship or have them attend Sunday school.
During the service
Nursery, Room 101 (birth to age 3), open before worship begins.
All other children start in the sanctuary with their families and are dismissed before the sermon to the Fellowship Room, where teachers sign them in to class.
PreK and kindergarten, Room 104, stay in class until the service ends.
Grades 1 and 2 (Room 103) and grades 3 and 4 (Room 102) return for communion and sit with their families.
What children learn

Our curriculum, Ligonier Ministries' Growing in God's Word, points children to Christ and teaches the truths of the Bible through questions and answers, with Scripture memory along the way. Each Sunday PreK through grade 2 review the First Catechism, and grades 3 through 5 review the Westminster Shorter Catechism.
A list of Sunday school teachers and the rotation schedule is posted on the bulletin board above the drinking fountain. Children's ministry pamphlets are in the church foyer.

data.title: Men's Ministry
data.summary: A monthly Saturday study, outings, and an annual retreat for the men of the church.

$media.alt: The men of Grace Church gathered on the patio

children.text: There is a special blessing when men come together in fellowship. We are called to be the spiritual leaders of our homes and church, and we are best able to do that as we build real relationships with one another and share our joys and victories as well as our trials and fears. By meeting together, the iron sharpening iron of Proverbs becomes a reality.

We meet the first Saturday of each month at 7:30 am in the Fellowship Hall, starting with coffee, fellowship, and prayer before we study. We are currently reading John Calvin's Institutes of the Christian Religion.
We also have outings for fun and fellowship (barbecues, movie nights, volleyball, hockey games) and an annual men's retreat. All men are welcome, including young men from junior high up.

data.title: Summer Retreat
data.summary: A summer camp for students from incoming 6th graders through outgoing 12th graders.

$media.alt: Students at an archery range at summer camp

children.text: The summer retreat is a great time of growing in faith through the study of God's Word, praying together, and worshiping in song. Students strengthen and make the friendships that are so vital to pressing on in the faith, with a whole lot of fun along the way.
Watch the news page for this year's dates and cost.

data.title: Vacation Bible School
data.summary: A week each summer of games, crafts, and learning the glories of God in Scripture, for kids 4 years old through 5th grade.

$media.alt: Children raising their hands during a lesson

children.text: Each summer we spend a week of mornings learning the glories of our God in Scripture, with games, crafts, activities, and tasty treats. All kids from 4 years old through 5th grade are welcome, and VBS is free.
This year's VBS, Emerald Crossing: An Irish Adventure through Psalm 23, ran July 20 to 24, 2026. Watch the news page for next summer's dates.
